mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as monetary policy eases.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 0.10%, it signals a shift toward monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS > 0.10, or the directional accuracy of the signal is below 55%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in unemployment rate and declines in nonfarm payrolls indicate a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In strong economic growth regimes (GDPC1 growth > 2.5% annualized), rising consumer spending (RSAFS growth) accelerates corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.5% and RSAFS growth is positive, or the Rank IC for the signal in this regime is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate over the past 3 months signals weakening labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where UNRATE has risen for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 7.0%, it indicates a severe labor market contraction that depresses consumer confidence and corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where UNRATE > 7.0, or the directional accuracy of the signal is below 55%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicate a supply shock that increases input costs and reduces corporate margins, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO falls and CPIAUCSL rises, or the Rank IC for the interaction is below 0.03 over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In manufacturing slowdown regimes (INDPRO growth rate below 0.5% annualized), declining industrial production signals reduced corporate activity and lower earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where INDPRO growth is below 0.5% annualized, or the Rank IC for the signal in this regime is below 0.03.
